breakthrough: Long-running work follows the best available hardware
lane: Provider, device, research, and remote-compute fleet control
outcome: Move active jobs between devices as connectivity, cost, and performance change

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Roaming Workload Scheduler Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Roaming Workload Scheduler Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed entities, capabilities, jobs, events, state transitions, and outputs required to move active jobs between devices as connectivity, cost, and performance change, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for nodes, providers, devices, remote execution, research workloads, and resilient edge operations; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Roaming Workload Scheduler Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: move active jobs between devices as connectivity, cost, and performance change.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Roaming Workload Scheduler Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Roaming Workload Scheduler Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using distributed scheduling, federated search, capability discovery, energy models, and fault prediction.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Roaming Workload Scheduler Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the fleet globe, node cockpit, workload map, and remote experiment terminal, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Roaming Workload Scheduler into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Roaming Workload Scheduler Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Roaming Workload Scheduler Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: Long-running work follows the best available hardware. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.
